text:
alex: FYI customer 'finline' in us-west-2 is seeing a burst of 429s since ~2025-06-12T09:03Z. They say it's intermittent but high frequency, ~4k RPM for a few 10-30s windows then back down. Request IDs in logs: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c4e. Can we triage?

marta: Thanks — can you paste one raw response + a sample request payload (no PII)? Also which model + route?

alex: model=gpt-small-q4; route=/v1/streams; sample curl (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"input":"price check","stream":true}' \\n  -v
```
Response headers: `x-redwood-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d`
Response body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","status":429,"message":"rate limit exceeded"}`

sam: quick checks — does this look like RPM (requests/min) or TPM (tokens/min) cap hit? Customer said "requests", but streaming can multiply token usage. Can you share per-tenant metrics snapshot (last 10m) and whether they use many concurrent streams?

alex: customer reports many short-lived parallel streams from a fleet of worker pods (cron-ish jobs) hitting at top-of-minute. Per-tenant metrics (10m window): peak RPM=4200, sustained RPM baseline=300. Token usage spiky but most spikes are short.

ratecap-bot: [ratecap] tenant=finline event=throttle window_start=2025-06-12T09:03:10Z window_end=2025-06-12T09:03:40Z limit_type=RPM limit=3000 observed=4200 drop_count=1200

jen: sounds like a classic alignment/heartbeat/cron fanout. Short-term options: 1) issue a temporary quota bump (if allowed) 2) enable tenant-level burst window smoothing / refill smoothing 3) ask client to add jitter/exponential backoff + cap concurrency. Long-term: recommend batching or a coordinator to stagger requests.

marta: For the short term I can request a +50% RPM bump for 24h while they deploy smoothing. Need tenant id and a link to the customer ticket. Who will contact the customer with mitigation steps?

alex: I'll draft the response. For triage — check ratecap logs and token-bucket occupancy on the gateway. Commands: `sudo rg "tenant=finline" /var/log/redwood/ratecap.log | tail -n 80` and `redis-cli -p 6379 HGETALL ratecap:finline` (gives refill timestamps). Example log lines we pulled:
```
2025-06-12T09:03:12Z INFO tenant=finline req_id=r-0a1b2c3d tokens_requested=1 bucket_remain=0 limit=3000 action=drop
2025-06-12T09:03:13Z INFO tenant=finline req_id=r-0a1b2c4e tokens_requested=3 bucket_remain=0 limit=3000 action=drop
2025-06-12T09:03:14Z INFO tenant=finline req_id=r-0a1b2c5f tokens_requested=1 bucket_remain=0 limit=3000 action=drop
```

sam: Those lines show bucket_remain=0 during the window => refill pacing is too coarse for their traffic shape. If we have per-second bursting disabled they get clobbered. We can enable smoothing to allow minor short spikes (smoothing trades some throughput for lower drop tail).

jen: Also check whether they have multiple API keys across pods — that can bypass per-key connection limits and increase concurrent streams. If so, suggest migrating to a pooled connector or set per-worker client-side rate limits.

marta: Action items: 1) alex to ask customer for one example request trace + client concurrency numbers; 2) sam to prepare an enable request for burst-smoothing on tenant finline; 3) jen to draft best-practice note for customer (jitter/backoff and max-parallel=10) ; 4) I will request a temporary RPM bump (+1500) for 24h if vendor support approves.

alex: pinging customer in ticket: "we're seeing short top-of-minute bursts that exceed your RPM window. Immediate options: stagger cron jobs, add jitter, or we can temporarily increase your RPM while you roll a fix. Please share representative client logs and how many worker pods/threads you run." Will provide sample curl and ask for request-id samples.

marta: I started the quota-bump workflow (Case #SR-7752). If support approves, I'll provision and post back here. ETA ~45-120m depending on approvals.

ratecap-bot: [action] quota_bump_request submitted tenant=finline request_id=sr-7752 amount=+1500 duration=24h submitted_by=marta

sam: If you want to prove repro quickly, you can run a controlled synthetic: a script that opens N concurrent streams for 20s at top-of-minute to mimic their workers. Example: `for i in {1..40}; do curl -s ... & done` with sleep to align to minute. Use a staging tenant first.

jen: also note: streaming endpoints multiply concurrent token consumption; for short spikes TPM may not be the limiting factor but concurrent token bursts can still overflow the bucket. Recommend we set a temporary rule: drop at 10 concurrent streams per API key to protect platform while we fix. Thoughts?

marta: Good point. I'll add a short-lived protective rule after approval.

alex: Thanks all — I'll update the customer with steps and collect traces. Leaving this thread open; will post the final status once quota bump outcome is known. :thumbsup:
